paragraphs.text: No. The filing representative cannot attest for the applicant or owner and cannot submit this job filing. The applicant must complete the Applicant of Record’s Attestation with an electronic signature before submission; the owner must complete the Owner’s Attestation to authorize the applicant to submit and acknowledge review of the filing. Filing representatives may enter and view filing information, but the guidance says they cannot submit filings or permits.

After the applicant and owner complete their own attestations, the applicant must review the filing, provide the final electronic signature, and officially submit it electronically to the Department. A filing representative can use Preview to File to identify what remains incomplete before the applicant submits. If the Owner Type is Condo Unit Owner or Co-Op Tenant-Shareholder, the Board representative must also log in and attest, and both the owner’s and Board representative’s attestations are required before the filing can proceed.

missingFacts: The Owner Type is not provided. If it is Condo Unit Owner or Co-Op Tenant-Shareholder, a Condo/Co-Op Board representative’s attestation is also required before the filing can proceed.

issues.detail: The answer says the owner must complete the Owner’s Attestation but omits the guidance’s material condition that the owner must be logged in using the same email address entered in the filing’s Owner Information.

paragraphs.text: Use a subsequent filing under the existing job number, not a new unrelated job number. DOB guidance says all filings for the same construction project should share the job number, with an alphabetic/numeric extension for filing type and sequence. A subsequent filing permits new scope and work types on the same property, and its applicant may differ from the initial applicant. It functions as a separate application and may have a different review type. The initial GC filing must be submitted—not remain in pre-filing status—before the subsequent filing can be initiated and submitted; the FAQ says it may be submitted until an LOC is issued for the initial filing.

For this path, select the Subsequent Filing action from the initial (I1) filing. The plumbing filing is processed separately: it can be permitted before the initial filing is permitted. Completion treatment depends on the initial job type: generally, an LOC is requested separately for each initial and subsequent filing; but for an NB or Alteration-CO filing, the supplied FAQ says no LOC is requested for the subsequent filing, which remains Permit Entire while only the I1 changes to CO issued. The facts do not identify the initial job type, so the applicable completion branch cannot be selected.

missingFacts: Whether the initial GC filing is an NB or Alteration-CO filing, which determines the supplied guidance on LOC treatment for the plumbing subsequent filing.
evidenceLimitations: The supplied FAQ states that subsequent filings are initiated and submitted after the initial filing is submitted, while another FAQ answer discusses a subsequent filing already in pre-filing status and recommends completing as much of I1 as possible before creating it. These passages do not resolve whether creation before I1 submission is permitted; they do establish that submission requires I1 to be submitted.

issues.detail: The statement that the initial filing must be submitted before the subsequent filing can be initiated is too broad: the supplied FAQ addresses submission after I1 submission but also refers to a subsequent filing in pre-filing status and does not resolve whether creation before I1 submission is permitted.
